lines.text: Do you know how walkie-talkies work? They're tiny radio stations that take turns.
Press the button, and your voice becomes a radio wave, sent out on one frequency, called a channel.
Every walkie-talkie on the same channel picks it up, and turns the wave back into sound.
But the button switches yours from listening to sending, and everyone shares that one channel. So only one person can talk at a time. That's why people say, over.
The signal is weak, so the range is usually just a few kilometres. Hills and buildings cut it even shorter.
Soldiers carried the first ones during World War Two.
Orbi Nearby works on a similar idea, locally. Phones on the same Wi-Fi find each other, with no login and no pairing.
